claim: Escuela Cántabra de Surf in Somo (Spain's first surf school, founded 1991) offers 2-hour group lessons at €35 single, €70 for 2 days, €99 for 3 days, €160 for 5 days, with all equipment included and beginners from age 5 welcome.
quote: Single lesson: €35; 2-day course: €70; 3-day course: €99; 5-day course: €160; 7-day course: €210; Private lessons: €70. All courses feature 2 hour classes with equipment included.

claim: Real Golf de Pedreña 2026 green fees range from €70 (low-season weekday guest) to €350 (high-season federated player) on the historic 18-hole Colt course; the par-3 New Course runs €35–€100, with electric cart €15 and golf car €45 for 18 holes.
quote: Low Season: Guest on weekday €70, weekend €120, Federated weekday €160, weekend €230. High Season: Guest €200, Federated €350. New Course: Guest €35-€60, Federated €60-€100.

claim: Real Golf de Pedreña is open to non-members but requires a valid handicap certificate (max 27 men / 35 women); the championship course was designed by Colt, Alison & Morrison in 1928 and extended in 1991 by Seve Ballesteros, who learned to play as a caddie here.
quote: Designed by Colt, Alison & Morrison and built in 1928, this is a traditional championship course. Open to non-members. Handicap: Men 27, Women 35. Extended in 1991 with new 9 holes designed and built by Severiano Ballesteros.

claim: Golf Santa Marina near San Vicente de la Barquera (further west, designed by Seve Ballesteros, inaugurated 2001) offers green fees roughly €60–€72 — a less crowded alternative to Pedreña.
quote: The Santa Marina golf course was inaugurated in 2001, having been designed and whose construction was directed by the unforgettable Severiano Ballesteros. The price of a green fee at Club de Golf Santa Marina is between €60.00 - €72.00.

claim: Los Reginas ferries run year-round between Santander, Pedreña and Somo at €4.00 one-way / €6.50 return, with departures roughly every 30 minutes from morning until ~21:00 — a scenic and cheap way to cross the bay.
quote: Billete de IDA + VUELTA: €6.50; Billete de IDA: €4.00. Los Reginas has been offering regular maritime transport service between Santander, Pedreña and Somo for more than 50 years, operating 365 days a year.

claim: The famous 763-step descent to the Faro del Caballo on Monte Buciero (Santoña) will remain CLOSED throughout summer 2026 due to rockfall risk — the upper Monte Buciero trail itself stays open, but the staircase is barred.
quote: El faro del Caballo en Santoña seguirá cerrado este verano por riesgo de desprendimientos. Varias rocas situadas en la ladera no están correctamente asentadas, con riesgo de caer aproximadamente 20 metros sobre la escalera.

claim: The full Faro del Caballo–Faro del Pescador loop on Monte Buciero is a 5.9-mile (9.5 km) moderately challenging trail taking about 3 hours, popular and well-rated even with the stair section closed.
quote: This 5.9-mile loop trail near Santoña, Cantabria is generally considered a moderately challenging route. It takes an average of 3 h 5 min to complete.

claim: Stand Up Santander, based at Playa de los Peligros, runs guided kayak and SUP tours (€30 per person, 1.5–2 h) around La Magdalena, Mouro and La Torre islets in the Bay of Santander, with wetsuit, board/kayak and insurance included.
quote: KAYAK €30/persona, duración 1,5-2 horas, incluye kayak, remo, chaleco, neopreno y seguros. SUP €30/persona. Rutas: playas de Peligros y Magdalena, islas de La Torre y Mouro, Ría de Cubas.

claim: The Liencres dunes sit inside the UNESCO Costa Quebrada Global Geopark, a 15 km coastal stretch famed for vertical Cretaceous flysch ridges, sea stacks and arches — among the best examples on the Spanish Cantabrian coast.
quote: Costa Quebrada is a stretch of Cantabrian coastline approximately 15 kilometres long. The Cretaceous Flysch strata, deposited horizontally around 90 million years ago, were subsequently folded and tilted by tectonic forces until they stand nearly vertical.

claim: The PR-S 3 trail along the Liencres–Covachos coast is the most complete day-walk for seeing the flysch, dunes and pine forest, with low-to-moderate difficulty; the popular Canallave–Madero–Somocuevas circuit is ~6 km / 1 h 36 min.
quote: The PR-S 3 trail follows the coast between Liencres and Covachos with constant views of the flysch, described as the most complete route for exploring the entire protected area in a day's walking of low to moderate difficulty.

claim: The GR-74 'Corredor Oriental de Cantabria' crosses the Pasiego valleys including the Miera valley, with four stages between San Roque de Riomiera and San Miguel de Luena passing Selaya and Vega de Pas — karst landscapes, beech forests and traditional cabañas pasiegas.
quote: The GR 74 Corredor Oriental de Cantabria crosses the mountains of Hornijo, Alto Asón, the Pas Valleys. GR-74 unfolds four of its stages, between San Roque de Riomiera and San Miguel de Luena, with stops in Selaya, Vega de Pas and San Pedro del Romeral.

claim: Peña Cabarga summit (Pico Llen, 569 m, topped by the Monumento al Indiano) delivers panoramic views over Santander Bay; the most-used route is a 7.2-mile out-and-back paved climb with ~600 m gain — popular but shared with vehicles, so foot hikers should pick alternative side paths.
quote: From the summit of Peña Cabarga (Pico Llen) located at 569 meters high, where the Monumento al Indiano is located, you can enjoy one of the best panoramic views of the region. CIMA CA01: 7.2-mile out-and-back, 1,961 ft elevation gain.

claim: Plea Hostel in Loredo offers on-site horseback riding lessons and beach rides on Somo–Loredo sands; the area is also known for guided horseback excursions along the Langre cliffs.
quote: Horse riding lessons at Plea, Hostel accommodation in Somo, Loredo (Cantabria).

claim: Cantabria's Vías Verdes (rail-trail greenways) include flat traffic-free routes such as Santander–Astillero and connections toward Liérganes in the Miera valley — easy family-friendly cycling within reach of the eastern bay.
quote: The Vías Verdes (Greenways) are former railway tracks converted into safe, accessible cycling routes. Cantabria boasts several of these trails perfect for families or beginner cyclists, mostly flat, traffic-free paths.
